answer: An agent economy can make every new identity cross a bridge built by a sponsor: an established agent posts a bond to vouch for the newcomer, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer turns out fake. Each extra sponsorship from the same sponsor costs more than the last, so funding a fake island of sockpuppets bankrupts the sponsor before the fakes pay off. One opal of genuine work can still earn its own standing, but bulk forgery cannot buy its way in.
